Proteins and current categories: CTAG1A: CTA; CTAG1B: CTA; CTAG2: CTA
Serious / severe events: Fatal cardiac arrest, day 161. Guillain-Barre / inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy.
Clinical interpretation: No grade 4-5 event was attributed to peptide-specific recognition of normal tissue. Grade 4 cytopenias occurred; one late cardiac death remained potentially treatment-related without an established specificity mechanism.

Serious / severe events: Grade 4 transaminitis during a grade 3 CRS episode.
Clinical interpretation: No treatment-related deaths after IMA203 infusion were reported. Severe cytopenias and CRS occurred; no clinical renal toxicity was seen despite weak reactivity in one in-vitro renal donor.

Serious / severe events: Fatal aplastic anemia, day 55. Fatal ischemic cerebrovascular accident, day 17.
Clinical interpretation: Two possibly treatment-related deaths occurred: aplastic anemia and ischemic stroke. Marrow evaluation did not support MAGE-A4-directed injury; high-dose conditioning and inflammation were considered contributors. No grade 5 adverse events or treatment-related deaths were reported; severe cytopenias and mostly low-grade CRS remained important regimen toxicities.

Serious / severe events: Fatal cardiac injury with titin cross-recognition.
Clinical interpretation: Fatal cardiac injury was attributed to T-cell cross-recognition, with titin identified as the likely unintended antigen.
Severe cytopenias and one grade 3 CRS occurred. No on-target/off-tumor toxicity was observed; fatal dyspnea was considered unrelated.

Serious / severe events: Grade 4 CRS. Fatal marrow aplasia, sepsis and respiratory distress after repeat infusion.
Clinical interpretation: One grade 4 CRS and one treatment-related death after repeat infusion/intensified conditioning. Investigations favored conditioning over MAGE-A10-mediated marrow injury.

Proteins and current categories: CTAG1A: CTA; CTAG1B: CTA; CTAG2: CTA
Serious / severe events: Steroid-responsive lung injury with TCR-T infiltration.
Clinical interpretation: One grade 3 lung injury with TCR-T infiltration; resolved with steroids. Authors favored cytokine-mediated capillary leak but could not exclude normal-peptide recognition.
